newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-OLYMPIC CHAMPION HOYER-LARSEN IN COMMAND.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-OLYMPIC CHAMPION HOYER-LARSEN IN COMMAND.

text.p: Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen of Denmark cruised through his opening match at the world badminton championships on Tuesday, crushing Russian Artur Khachaturjan 15-6 15-5.
The world number two was on court only 27 minutes, taking command at 5-3 and racing away with the next eight points.
All the seeds survived, although English champion Peter Knowles threatened an upset when he claimed the opening game 15-9 and led 4-2 in the second against ninth seed Budi Santoso.
But the Indonesian hit back, squaring the match 15-11 and raced through the decider without conceding a point.
Top seed Dong Jiong of China started his bid for a first world title with a 15-6 15-3 victory over South Korean Jang Chun-woong.
Defending champion Heryanto Arbi of Indonesia, seeded only 12, trounced Austria's Juergen Koch 15-1 15-6.
Ye Zhaoying and Gong Zhichao, who both helped China to retain the Sudirman Cup world team crown last week, experienced few problems in reaching the last 32.
Ye, All-England champion and world number one, was held at 5-4 by Sandra Dimbour of France in the opening game but pulled away to win 11-4 11-2.
Gong, who lost to Ye in the All-England final, was an equally convincing winner, defeating England's number one Julia Mann 11-3 11-0 in just 18 minutes.

Indonesia's Susi Susanti was similarly untroubled in clearing the first hurdle in her quest to regain the title she held in 1993. The fifth seed needed only 12 minutes to outclass Hong Kong's Ng Chin 11-4 11-1.
